az_mermaid_lagoon.blurb: Mermaid Lagoon is a small pocket of boulders in Euro Dog Valley, part of the Oak Flat bouldering zone in Queen Creek Canyon east of Phoenix. The problems sit in a dry wash below Hook Wall, so the setting is leafy and cool rather than exposed, and the shade is the main draw on warm days. The sixteen problems are all short and span roughly V0 to V4, split fairly evenly, which makes it a friendly stop for newer boulderers and anyone wanting a mellow circuit on volcanic rock. Getting in means a walk north from the Scatterbrain boulder, past the Titanic wall, and a drop down into the wash.

az_y2k.blurb: Y2K is a loop of boulders in Euro Dog Valley, within the Oak Flat bouldering zone of Queen Creek Canyon near Superior. Dense trees and brush make it easy to find shade when the weather warms up, and the boulders offer big faces and long, clean lines on volcanic rock. The sixteen problems here run from easy warm-ups through the mid-grades into serious hard territory, with a handful of problems in the double-digit V range, so strong climbers have projects while newcomers still have a few easier lines. The trail leaves Magma Mine Road a short way south of the Campground Boulder, where the guardrail ends.

az_piranha_flats_east.blurb: Piranha Flats - East is a compact bouldering spot on the plateau above Queen Creek Canyon, in the Oak Flat zone east of Phoenix. A few free-standing boulders and narrow passageways between them hold most of the problems, and most of them face north, so it works as a choice on warm days. There is also a short wall a little farther south. The sixteen problems are friendly: mostly V1 to V3, with a few at V4 and V5, which suits climbers building up to harder grades. From the neighboring western section it is only a couple of minutes on foot, following cairns on volcanic rock.

az_main_wall_right.blurb: Main Wall Right is the eastern stretch of the tall Main Wall in the High Rappel area of Granite Gardens, in the Granite Dells just north of Prescott. The wall is named for the steel rings along the top of its steepest section and sits close to the highway. Climbing is mostly traditional with a few bolted lines and one top-rope, on medium-grained desert granite that can feel grainy. The sixteen routes lean hard: one easy line, a few at 5.10, then a solid block of 5.11 and 5.12, with one at 5.13. It suits experienced leaders more than beginners. The approach climbs railroad tie steps from the parking area and swings around the formation's west side.

az_western_bouldering_area.blurb: The Western Bouldering Area is a collection of large boulders beside the main trail at Echo Canyon on Camelback Mountain, right in the middle of Phoenix. It is a short walk from the trailhead lot: follow the main trail a couple of hundred paces to a big pocketed boulder, then take the climbers' path branching left. Many chalked traverses and problems here are on the easy side, and the sixteen problems run from V0 to V6, mostly V1 to V3. The rock is only fair in quality but solid enough to climb. It is a handy after-work spot for beginners and a warm-up for others, though the lot is small and fills early.

az_laser_wall.blurb: Laser Wall is an alcove in the Oak Flat zone of Queen Creek Canyon, east of Phoenix, with one wall facing south and another facing north. Most of its walls have top-rope anchors, and brush and boulders fill the alcove, so finding the cleanest line can take a try or two. Nearly all of the sixteen climbs are boulder problems on volcanic rock, with a single top-rope route. The grades are wide: a few in the V4 to V6 range, a cluster from V7 to V9, and a handful of V10 and up, plus a top-rope in the 5.13 range. It is a place for strong climbers. The approach follows a wash from the road.

az_siberia_sherman_wall.blurb: Siberia is a small group of dark-streaked walls on the Black Mountains side of Golden Valley, outside Kingman in northwestern Arizona. The district as a whole is mostly bolted climbing from about 5.7 to 5.12, with sunny mornings and shady afternoons, so you can move around to follow the shade. Siberia itself holds an even split of sport and trad lines, nearly half of them 5.9 and many of the rest at 5.11, with a couple at 5.12. Reaching it takes a quarter-hour walk on burro trails toward the black cliffs from the third approach, and a vehicle with some clearance is probably needed on the dirt road.
